w: The climax of Swamishri’s 5-day stay in Bhuj was the celebration of Shri Hari Jayanti – the birthday of Lord Swaminarayan.
Swamshri travelled by plane and reached Bhuj at 11.01 a.m. A grand welcome was accorded to Swamishri with a motorcade of 108 cars and 11 turban-donned devotees on motorcycles.

In the evening assembly, the Mahant of Ramji mandir in Vandhhaya, Pujya Haridasji said, "We are very fortunate to have the darshan of Pramukh Swamiji. If we accept him as the sailor of our life’s boat then he will see us through the ocean of life. I am seeing Pramukh Swamiji for the first time..."
Swamishri, in his blessings, said, "Kuch-Bhuj is a pilgrim place. Bhagwan Swaminarayan has blessed this land eight times. Ramanand Swami had also been here.

"Inner progress for spiritual development is a very important thing. As long as we fail to remove our baser instincts and bad nature we will keep on suffering from unhappiness, frustration and pain. By preserving our fundamental values and culture we will experience peace and happiness. The great acharyas and incarnations of God came on earth to remind us of our true purpose and duties in life.

"We find there is mundane happiness in America but there is no peace of mind. There is killing and conflicts everywhere. In spite of wealth yet people cannot sleep. They have to take sleeping pills. In the west, people are indulging in worldly pleasures and that is why they cannot experience peace and happiness. Happiness lies in God and in the atma. And to make people aware of that knowledge and realise the atma Shriji Maharaj came to this world..."

After Swamishri's evening dinner, a sadhu asked, "Once in Sarangpur, Bapubhai asked Shastriji Maharaj as to which matter did his joy and pleasure (rajipo) rested in. To this Shastriji Maharaj replied that he was pleased in the making of Akshar Purushottam mandirs and in the propagation of the Akshar Purushottam philosophy. Then from the life of Yogiji Maharaj one can conclude that his joy lay in having harmony, friendship and unity. So at present in which principle does your joy (rajipo) lie in?"

Swamishri explained, "Shriji Maharaj has said that His principle is the same in all things and it follows like a thread in a needle. This principle is that of ekantik dharma, to become brahmarup and to offer devotion to God. Shastriji Maharaj did not differ from this principle of ekantik dharma of Shriji Maharaj. For this he desired that everyone should understand the knowledge of Akshar and Purushottam, establish mandirs and spread that mode of worship (upasana). In this lay his joy which was not different from the principle of Shriji Maharaj.

"Then Yogiji Maharaj said that to promote this principle of upasana harmony, friendship and unity were necessary. So it was not different from the principle of Shriji Maharaj. It is we who differentiate that is this true or is that true..., and in this way we go on elaborating but none of the principles are different. They are the same principles that Shriji Maharaj had established. To spread His principle (of ekantik dharma) it is necessary to have mandirs and to increase Satsang it is necessary to have harmony, friendship and unity. So we have to do the same. What I say is not different from the principles established. They are the same that were propagated by Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj." Swamishri's answer of a common principle and aim resolved the expectation of any other new principle that aspirants generally expect to hear and become enlighgtened with.
Today marked the 10th patotsav (mandir inauguration anniversary) of the Badalpur mandir.
At 10.00 a.m. Swamishri performed the mahapuja held to commemorate this occasion. A beautiful annakut was offered to Thakorji and at the end Swamishri performed the Patotsav arti.

A devotee telephoned Swamishri and expressed his fears about his dying wife, “Swamishri, the doctors have lost hope for my wife and say that now everything is in God’s hands. Do shower your blessings so that she recovers.”

Swamishri replied, “You should accept whatever God wishes. The human body is perishable. It will die at any time. Believe it to be Maharaj’s wish and remain happy. Presently, your wife is going through pain and suffering, so if she goes to God’s abode she will be happier. You are a spiritually knowledgeable person. You have satsang in your soul and your wife too has satsang in her life. She will become engaged in the service of Maharaj in Akshardham. When the doctors have lost hope there is no need to think otherwise. Have patience and faith. Maharaj is the all-doer. Whatever He does will be for the best.”
Swamishri consolidated the spiritual faith of the devotee to enable him to accept the reality of life.

The sadhus sitting in the rupchoki were singing: 'Je je harie karyu het, evu kare kon apne re; mat tat saga samet, manya sanehi bholapane re...' (The love Hari showed, who else shows us such love? Mother, father and relatives we took as loved ones in our innocence).

Explaining the meaning of innocence, Swamishri said, "Those who were not ours we took (in a worldly way) as mother and father. To believe it though it is not so, to understand it though it is not, that is called innocence. Once we take (spiritually, God and the Sant) as our true mother and father, we must forget all that."
Nilkanthseva Swami said, "Those (worldly parents) did not know how to show true love, and you do, so everyone has come here."
"That is true," Swamishri agreed.

Swamishri comes every day for darshan of Hanumanji and Ganpatiji. While Swamishri is doing darshan, the sadhus keep saying various inspiring sentences. Mostly it is Brahmasetu Swami who says them. Today he was sitting at the back, and a sadhu sitting in front of him was saying, 'Whoever keeps love for God and the Sant, everyone will call him.'
Swamishri heard the sentence, but seeing Brahmasetu Swami sitting at the back, he said, "Why are you at the back today?"
Brahmasetu Swami said, "Today it was his turn to speak, so I seated him in front."
"Very good. Keep such courtesy." Swamishri taught courtesy.
